title: Three plans for one query: parameter sensitive plan optimization at work
prompt: A developer saw 'three plans for one query' in a Query Store report and asks for the fastest plan to be forced, or
for OPTION (RECOMPILE). Facts: the query has one dispatcher plan and three query variants
(sys.query_store_query_variant has three rows for the parent query). The variant for @Status = 'Pending' seeks
IX_Orders_Status and runs in 12 ms. The variant for 'Paid' runs in 0.9 s. The variant for 'Shipped' scans and runs in
2.1 s; that case runs four times a day and its target is 5 s. Each variant has had one plan for 30 days, with no
regression and no forced plan. The Orders table has three nonclustered indexes and takes about 2.1M status updates a
day; the owner does not want another index for a query that meets its targets.
data_notes: Azure SQL Database, General Purpose Gen5, 8 vCores, compatibility level 160. READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON. Query Store READ_WRITE. Collation SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. All foreign keys are trusted. Statistics: auto create and auto update ON; a nightly job updates Orders, OrderLines and Payments with FULLSCAN.

Orders: 30M rows, 2016 to now, ~12k per day now. The 25 partner customers own ~9M orders (30%), up to 1.2M each. Other customers average ~10 orders (max ~400). The density estimate for CustomerID is ~15 rows. Status: Shipped 83.8%, Cancelled 7%, Paid 6%, Returned 3%, Pending 0.2% (~60k rows, all from the last 72 hours). SalesChannel: Web 62%, Store 20%, Partner 12%, Phone 6%. PromoCode is NULL for 85%. ShipRegionID is NULL for Store pickups (~20%). OrderDate is datetime2(7); Partner and Store imports stamp one timestamp on a whole batch, so many orders of one customer share an OrderDate.

Customers: 2.0M rows. Tier S = 1.85M, G = ~150k, P = 25 partner accounts (CustomerID 1 to 25). IsActive = 1 for 88%. Email is NULL for ~9% (~180k rows, ~160k of them active). About 2% of non-NULL emails are shared by two or more customer rows (households). ReferredByCustomerID is non-NULL for 18%; 312 rows are self-referrals (ReferredByCustomerID = CustomerID, CustomerID 500001 to 500312). AccountNumber always matches 'AC' + 10 digits (CHECK constraint).
baseline_sql: JOIN qe.Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID

traps.why: The three plans are the feature: one per data volume. Forcing one of them, or the parent, takes the right plan away from the other two groups.
OPTION (RECOMPILE) replaces three cached plans that already fit with a compile on every call.
example_sql: JOIN qe.Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID

traps.why: Turning the feature off, for the database or with a hint, brings back one plan for all three volumes.
traps.example_sql: ALTER DATABASE SCOPED CONFIGURATION SET PARAMETER_SENSITIVE_PLAN_OPTIMIZATION = OFF;

min_improvement.basis: No change is the answer. A candidate is measured only to show that no status group gets more than 10% worse.

key.reference_notes: Several plans for one parent query are expected when sys.query_store_query_variant has rows. Judge each variant against its own target.
